How Jimdo Works

Jimdo is a website builder and hosting service based in Hamburg, Germany. The company was founded in 2007 and has gone through several iterations of its website builder. In the most recent iteration, Jimdo has done away with templates and uses AI to help you launch a new website.

Jimdo is best suited for anyone who wants to build a custom website as quickly as possible. It’s also fairly inexpensive and is a good budget option if you don’t mind giving up some control over your site design.

Using Jimdo

It’s quick and easy to design a website with Jimdo. It uses an automated site designer to help you get started, and then you can customize your site in page sections rather than content element by content element. While this doesn’t give you a ton of flexibility, it’s ideal for getting up and running as fast as possible.

Jimdo Features and Tools

Web Hosting

All Jimdo plans include web hosting, although storage and bandwidth limits vary by plan. You also get a free SSL certificate and a free domain for one year with paid plans.

Logo Designer

Jimdo has a logo designer to help you shape your online business’s brand. Just enter your business’s name and category, and Jimdo will instantly suggest logo designs. There are several options for customizing your design, and you can download the final product as an SVG file.

How to Create a Website with Jimdo

The process of creating a website with Jimdo is a little different from that of other website builders. Instead of selecting a template, you’ll answer questions about your business and the types of pages you want to include on your website. Based on this, Jimdo will use AI to suggest several personalized website options. Just choose the one you like best to begin customizing it with the page editor.

Jimdo doesn’t let you drag and drop individual content elements like text boxes or images onto your pages. Rather, you can only add page blocks, each of which contains multiple content elements. For example, a block might include an image and text box, a banner, or an image gallery. Jimdo has dozens of premade blocks, so it’s easy to build up your site content quickly. You have very little control over the layout of each block, although you can show or hide individual content elements within blocks.

Notably, Jimdo also doesn’t give you much control over your site’s styles. You can customize your color palette, fonts, and button shape, but that’s about it. There are no options to modify block padding, the navigation bar layout, or your site’s footer. All Jimdo sites are mobile-responsive.

Jimdo’s approach towards website design will appeal much more to those who want to get up and running quickly than to those who want tight control over their site’s design. It’s straightforward to create a custom site in minutes, but your options for creating a unique look or layout are very limited.

Adding Multimedia to Your Jimdo Website

Jimdo lets you import images and videos from your computer, Facebook, and Instagram. If you opt to import images when first setting up your site, the AI designer will incorporate them into the sites it suggests for you. Jimdo saves all of your images to a media library, making it easy to add alt text and reuse them anywhere on your site.

Jimdo also lets you add audio to your site via a link to Spotify or iTunes. However, there’s no way to add documents or PDFs.

Marketing Functionality with Jimdo Websites

Jimdo has very few marketing features. You can import images and videos from social media, but you can’t publish updates from your website automatically to your social media pages. In addition, Jimdo doesn’t support blogging or any email marketing or newsletter tools.

SEO Functionality & Add-Ons with Jimdo Websites

Paid Jimdo websites include SEO tools that help your site get discovered by Google. All sites are optimized for mobile, and you can click to have your site re-indexed by Google after you make major changes. In addition, you can edit meta titles and descriptions for all of your pages. Jimdo even offers personalized advice to help you maximize your site’s SEO potential.

Jimdo doesn’t offer its own analytics tools. Instead, the platform offers instructions for how to integrate with Google Analytics to monitor your site statistics.

Ecommerce

Jimdo is one of the cheapest platforms for building an Ecommerce site. We don’t love the Ecommerce features, but they perform well enough for basic storefronts.

You can design products using the same page editor as for the rest of your site. In fact, products are simply a type of block that you can add to any page. That gives you some flexibility, but it also means that Jimdo doesn’t let you add SKUs or track inventory. You also can’t or sell digital downloads or organize products into categories that visitors can search or filter.

That said, Jimdo does have a few handy storefront features. The Business plan lets you sell products on Facebook and Instagram, as well as create discount codes and product variants. You can also set up custom shipping rules. For payments, Jimdo integrates with PayPal and Square.

Jimdo Customer Support

Jimdo offers 24/7 customer support by email only. The company offers varying levels of responsiveness according to your plan: Grow, Basic, and Business customers can expect a response in under 4 hours, while Play and Start customers may wait 1-2 days for a response. Jimdo also has an extensive knowledge center you can access to read how-to articles and get insights on the platform.

Jimdo Pricing

Jimdo offers 5 plan options, including a free plan. Three of the plans are for basic websites, while 2 are for Ecommerce sites. All plans except the free plan include a free domain for 1 year. In addition, all Jimdo plans are paid annually and come with a 14-day money-back guarantee.

Jimdo vs WordPress.com

However, WordPress.com is much more expensive than Jimdo if you want to sell internationally or access plug-ins for marketing and SEO.

Jimdo vs Squarespace

products.mainContent:
Overview

Webador was established in the Netherlands in 2010 to provide beginner-friendly website-building solutions to European customers. It has grown from strength to strength since, adding ecommerce functionality in 2018, and it currently claims to service 77,000 customers.

The thing that makes Webador stand out from the competition is its simplicity. Everything from its price structure to its user interface is designed to provide you with a streamlined experience, and it succeeds at this goal.

There are a few self-help resources, including a simple getting-started guide, but don’t expect too much assistance building your website. The good news is that the builder is designed to be intuitive enough that you shouldn’t need assistance.

Webador is a decent option for anyone looking for an affordable, beginner-friendly website builder.

Using Webador

Creating a new Webador account is a very straightforward process. When you hit the signup button, you will be asked to enter an email address and password before being taken to the template selection page. After selecting a template, you will have the option to upgrade to a premium plan (with a simple, hassle-free checkout process) or stick with a free subscription.

On top of this, everything about Webador is intuitive and user-friendly. The main management dashboard enables you to view your websites (you can add more than one if required), and the editor contains loads of tools for customizing and configuring your site. Overall, you shouldn’t have any issues getting your new website online.

Webador Features and Tools

Webador is a basic website builder, but it offers a number of noteworthy tools that are worth being aware of.

Integrated Business Listings

Webador enables you to add a custom business listing to Google and Google Maps. This is an excellent way to gain visibility for your business, and it’s especially important for small, locally oriented companies.

Free Domain

All premium plans come with a free domain name. You can also import your own custom domain and link it to your website if required. Or, if you’re looking for a budget-friendly option, you can use the free plan with a free Webador-branded subdomain.

No Commission Fees

Webador offers 0% commission on all sales that are made through its Webshop online store interface. This is particularly attractive for small stores with low profit margins, as it takes away one of the costs you’d otherwise have to worry about.

Custom HTML

You can add custom HTML code to your Webador website. This enables you to embed custom elements, adjust your site design, and add your own code where required. Most people using Webador won’t have to worry about adding HTML snippets, but it’s a useful tool nonetheless.

How to Create a Website with Webador

During the account creation process, you will be asked to select a template to start your new Webador website. There are 42 pre-designed layouts to choose from, or you can start with a blank canvas and build your site from the ground up.

One thing we liked was that Webador clearly states that it enables you to change your template at any point in time. All designs are fully responsive on mobile, and you can view and edit both mobile and desktop versions of your site.

The Webador editor uses a section-based approach. This is a little inflexible, but it’s also pretty much foolproof, which makes it perfect for anyone without much design knowledge or experience.

To add new elements to your website, simply drag them from the menu on the left of the screen and drop them into an available position. It’s super easy to customize different elements—simply click them and follow the prompts—and global features can be personalized via the Design menu.

A small feature, but one that really makes a difference, is the small informational popups that appear when you hold your mouse over an editing tool or page element. You can preview your site before it goes live, and making it live is as simple as hitting the publish button.

On the downside, there are no design assistants or keyboard shortcuts. You also can’t migrate your site to another platform without completely rebuilding it. But overall, Webador performs admirably. It’s not the most powerful website builder on the market, but it’s a leading option for those looking for a fast, beginner-friendly solution.

Adding Multimedia to Your Webador Website

The Webador multimedia manager supports the upload of multiple files at a time. Most popular file formats are supported, including JPG, PNG, and GIF, and you can also upload files from a URL. Stock media is available through the Unsplash media library, but there’s no way to import images directly from social media or any other third-party platform.

Videos can be embedded from YouTube, and there’s a built-in YouTube search tool. You can only upload your own videos with a Pro subscription, and there’s a 5GB limit.

Webador doesn’t do badly on the multimedia front, but we would have liked to see the ability to import photos from a few more third-party sources.

Marketing Functionality With Webador Websites

Webador has no email marketing or newsletter functionality, but it does enable you to add a simple blog to your website. However, the blog manager is quite basic. You can add social media icons to your site, but there are no more advanced integrations. Simple blog analytics are available but don’t expect anything too fancy.

SEO Functionality & Add-Ons With Webador Websites

Webador has an excellent reputation as a website builder that’s great for search engine optimization (SEO). Websites built with it are fast and responsive, which are two major search engine ranking factors. You can also configure SEO settings for each page, blog post, and image. The built-in analytics are quite basic, but you can integrate Google Analytics and link to your Google Search Console to track the effectiveness of your SEO efforts.

Ecommerce

With a paid subscription, Webador enables you to create your own simple online store. There are a number of templates, and you can make basic customizations to its style and appearance. The native Webshop tool enables you to list products, accept online payments, and sell digital items. Webador does have basic inventory management and analytics tools, but it's not as powerful as ecommerce leaders like Shopify or Weebly.

Webador Customer Support

Webador only offers email support, which means that replies can be slightly slow. The team is responsive, but the nature of email means that you may have to wait a few hours or even a day before you get an answer to your question.

There is a fully searchable help center, but this is also somewhat limited. There’s only a small number of articles, and these are a little basic. On the plus side, there is a complete getting-started guide, along with a video that outlines the steps involved in creating your first website. There’s also a small number of FAQs answering simple questions.

Webador Pricing

Webador has a very clear price structure, with two premium subscription options and a free-forever plan. The free-forever plan comes with a branded .webador.com subdomain and limited extras, but it enables you to create a fully-functional website.

A Pro plan will cost you $1 per month for the first three months and $10 per month after this (discounted to $0 for the first three months and $8 per month thereafter with an annual subscription). It comes with a free domain name, support for an online store with up to 10 products, and a suite of extra tools like password protection and customizable forms.

The high-end Business plan also costs $1 per month for the first three months, but it increases to $20 per month after this ($0 and $16 with an annual subscription). This adds selling support for unlimited products and the ability to upload HD videos.

HubSpot’s CMS Hub offers streamlined website-building solutions that integrate seamlessly with the rest of the HubSpot ecosystem. It’s a little more confusing to use and much more expensive than Webador, but it offers much better email marketing, SEO, and ecommerce functionality. All in all, CMS Hub is perfect for those already using other HubSpot products, along with anyone else looking for a marketing-focused website builder.

Webador vs 123 Reg

Like Webador, 123 Reg is a popular option among website-building newbies who want to get online fast. It’s also quite intuitive and easy to use, and it’s based in Europe. 123 Reg is slightly lower-priced than Webador, but Webador’s editor performed better during our testing.

Webador vs Jimdo

Jimdo is also a beginner-friendly website builder that’s designed for those with little experience. It uses AI design tools to deliver a custom template for your business, and it has decent SEO tools. At the end of the day, Jimdo is a decent option. However, Webador is still our choice for anyone looking for a beginner-friendly, intuitive website building solution.

Bottom Line

All things considered, Webador offers streamlined website building solutions that are intuitive and require no prior tech experience. Its editor is very easy to use, and it enables you to add a simple blog and online store to your site.

Webador is also known for its decent SEO, and its prices are clear and quite competitive. If you’re looking for a website builder to create a new site for your small business or next project, we’d suggest signing up for Webador’s free plan and giving it a try.

articles.mainContent:
Website builders are essential for creating a solid online presence, and WordPress is one of the most well-known CMS (content management systems) platforms in this domain. WordPress has many business plugins and features like advanced design tools, pre-built blocks, and SEO mechanisms. It's no wonder that over 40% of all websites use this builder.

But, while it's a popular option, it may not be the best fit for everyone. With my master's degree in economics and extensive experience as a legal and technical consultant, my team and I have compiled a comparative list of five top WordPress alternatives to help you build and launch your website in 2026.

Our 5 Best WordPress Alternatives in 2026:

  • Wix - Best WordPress alternative overall
  • IONOS - Best for building an online presence quickly
  • Shopify - Best for online store owners looking to grow their business
  • Jumdo - Best for creating a website easily and affordably
  • Squarespace - Best for Image-heavy websites

A Closer Look at the Best WordPress Alternatives in 2026

1. Wix

A powerful all-in website builder with 800+ templates to choose from

  • Best for - small businesses who want to build a website without a large budget
  • Starting price - From $16/month
  • Free version - Yes

Wix is my top recommendation if you're looking for a simpler, more intuitive alternative to WordPress. It has various customization options and a wide variety of Wix-designed templates. Its AI-powered design assistant also makes it easy for anyone to create a website.

The strength of Wix lies in its theme-based web design capabilities. With 800+ themes and a simple drag-and-drop editor, it allows for lots of design creativity, even if you're a beginner. Plus, there are dozens of Wix plugins for eCommerce sites to help you grow your online store.

What Makes Wix a Good Alternative to WordPress?

One significant advantage I've noticed is Wix's comprehensive managed hosting solutions, unlike WordPress, where you must take care of your hosting. Also, while I consistently have to update plugins on WordPress, Wix handles all updates automatically, saving me time and effort.

Pros

  • Offers a free-forever plan
  • Integrated features, including SEO tools and eCommerce solutions
  • AI-powered design assistant

Cons

  • Templates are not mobile-responsive
  • Can't alter the core source code of your website

2. IONOS

An intuitive website builder enabling you to launch quickly

  • Best for - Building an online presence quickly
  • Starting price - From $1/month
  • Free version - No

IONOS is one of the most straightforward site builders I've used, making it an excellent choice if you want to create and launch a website fast. It features an AI-powered text generator and a library of 17,000+ images, which can help you build your online presence in a matter of hours. With WordPress, you need to source your own images.

IONOS stands out for two reasons: It's got impressive eCommerce features, like social selling, a mobile app, and built-in metrics that automatically track, measure, and analyze various aspects of your website's performance.

What Makes IONOS a Good Alternative to WordPress?

WordPress has a large community and lots of information available online. But with IONOS, I get personalized customer care, including phone support. The platform is also easy to use and ideal for small business owners who want to get online fast and hassle-free. In my opinion, WordPress has a steeper learning curve.

Pros

  • Domain registration services
  • Robust eCommerce features
  • Cloud server leasing

Cons

  • Limited Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) provider options
  • No free option to transfer a website

3. Shopify

A comprehensive eCommerce platform with solid website creation tools

  • Best for - Online store owners looking to grow their business
  • Starting price - From $29/month
  • Free version - No

WordPress is among the best blogging platforms, but if you want to build a large online store, you need a platform like Shopify. It's an excellent choice if you want to grow your online store quickly. And if you'd like to benefit from both features, you can use them together.

Shopify offers top-notch eCommerce features, such as selling unlimited products, integrating with various marketplaces, and providing wholesale solutions for business-to-business (B2B) customers. That's why over 4 million users trust it for online selling.

What Makes Shopify a Good Alternative to WordPress?

While WordPress is undeniably a versatile CMS, I need to integrate it with an external platform to build an online store. In contrast, Shopify streamlines the process with its dedicated eCommerce functionalities. It also offers automatic website maintenance, which I don't have with WordPress.

Pros

  • Themes are mobile-responsive
  • Built-in payment gateway
  • Provides SSL certificates

Cons

  • Transaction fees may be a little high
  • Limited design freedom

4. Jimdo

Website builder that offers a drag-and-drop site-building experience

Best for - Creating a website easily and affordably

Starting price - from $0/ month

Free version - Yes

Jimdo provides most of what today’s site creator needs, and its automatic site creator, Dolphin, can do most of the work for you.

Jimdo’s free account only limits you by the amount of storage your site consumes, which is capped at 500MB, and the bandwidth is limited to 2GB. The Business plan includes online store functionality and premium support.

What Makes Jimdo a Good Alternative to WordPress?

While WordPress is a powerful platform, beginners may find it overwhelming. Jimdo’s user-friendly interface makes it easy for you to build your website without any coding knowledge. I also appreciate Jimdo's online store-building templates, which are helpful for entrepreneurs and small businesses.

Pros:

  • WYSIWYG (what you see is what you get)
  • Good site customization
  • Automatic site creator

Cons:

  • Jimdo logo only removed in higher-tier plans
  • Limited free version storage

5. Squarespace

A robust platform for creating a modern-looking website

  • Best for - Image-heavy websites
  • Starting price - From $16/month
  • Free version - No; 14-day free trial

Squarespace is one of my favorite website builders. Thanks to its beautiful templates and easy-to-use editor, you can create a stunning site—even without design experience. You can also use it to build a wide range of websites like blogs and online stores. You can even create an online portfolio using Squarespace's portfolio templates.

To make full use of the platform, I suggest you invest in high-quality images and professional product photos. Storage and bandwidth are unlimited, so you can even upload videos or animations at no extra cost.

What Makes Squarespace a Good Alternative to WordPress?

Having built websites on both platforms, I've found that Squarespace offers a more streamlined experience for those without coding or design experience. It has around 100 templates that are all professionally designed. WordPress has 11,000+ themes, but from what I've seen, their quality varies greatly.

Pros

  • Mobile-friendly templates
  • Powerful eCommerce and marketing features
  • Intuitive page editor

Cons

  • More expensive than other options
  • No phone support

What to Look For in a Website Builder

When you select a WordPress alternative app, service, or system, several key factors must be considered. Here's what you need to know before building your website:

  • Ease of use: The platform should be easy to use. You shouldn't need extensive technical knowledge or coding skills to create and manage your website.
  • Customization options: The service should have a variety of customization options, including themes, templates, and plugins. This will allow you to create a unique website that stands out.
  • Security: Your site builder needs robust security features to protect your website from hackers, malware, and other online threats. Check if it provides regular updates to ensure online safety.
  • Scalability: The service provider should allow your business to expand. Find out how it handles increased site traffic and if it offers additional features as your website grows.
  • Pricing: Your site builder price plan needs to suit your budget. Most providers offer various plans to choose from. Also, consider the cost of additional features and services you'll need, such as domain registration and hosting.
  • Support: The platform should offer reliable customer support to help you resolve any issues. Check the customer support availability hours, as some may not be available over the holidays. Others might only be accessible via text or chat.

How We Determined the Top WordPress Alternatives

Our team of experts, led by Melina Alexandrov, has conducted extensive research and testing to determine the best WordPress alternatives. Melina's qualifications and strong background in marketing lend themselves to insightful research.

The team’s combined expertise, experience, and qualifications make us well-suited for conducting these evaluations. We deeply understand the website-building industry and have conducted extensive research to ensure our evaluations are well-rounded and unbiased.

Our hands-on testing and research process integrates real user experiences, academic research, customer reviews, and industry insights. We evaluate each platform based on a set of key differentiating features (KDFs), including:

  • Ease of use: We evaluate how easy it is to use each platform, including the user interface, customization options, and overall user experience.
  • Design and templates: We evaluate the quality and variety of design templates available on each platform.
  • Features and functionality: We evaluate the features and functionality of each platform, including eCommerce capabilities, SEO tools, and integrations with other services.
  • Pricing and value: We evaluate the pricing and value of each platform, including the cost of each plan and the features included in each plan.
  • Customer support: We evaluate the quality and availability of customer support for each platform.

Our evaluation process provides a well-rounded and unbiased assessment of each platform. We are committed to providing our readers with credible and reliable information to help them make informed decisions.

Build a Website That Stands Out

WordPress is an excellent choice if you know your way around website building. But, it may not cater to everyone's needs. If you want to create a website quickly without code or need ways to create your site on a budget, these alternatives provide viable options.

This guide has showcased the strengths of various platforms, each tailored to different needs and expertise levels. The key takeaway is the importance of selecting a tool that aligns with your unique design and growth goals and offers ways to improve your user experience for a thriving website. Happy building!

FAQs

What is the best alternative to WordPress?

Wix is our best alternative for WordPress for it's features and affordability. But, the most suitable alternative to WordPress will largely depend on your specific needs for your website – be it a website, blog or online store.

Is WordPress free to use?

Yes, WordPress is free to use in its basic form. It's a blogging platform offering a variety of themes and plugins. However, premium plans are necessary to enhance a WordPress site with advanced features.

Can I migrate my existing WordPress site to another website builder?

Yes, migrating an existing WordPress site to another website builder is possible, but the process varies based on the new platform. Most major builders like Squarespace, Wix, and Shopify offer tools or services to assist in migration.

Is WordPress still relevant in 2026?

Yes, WordPress remains relevant in 2024 as a robust web hosting platform. It remains a popular choice for a range of websites. Its strength lies in its library of themes and plugins, customization options, and a strong community for support.

What is WordPress best for?

WordPress is best known for its versatility as a blogging platform and website builder. It offers a range of customization options through themes and plugins, making it useful for experienced bloggers and complex website creators.

articles.summary: Online courses are popular because creators can share their knowledge with the world with fewer limitations.
articles.mainContent:
If you want to monetize your website through online courses, you should definitely use Wix. It's one of the best places to sell your content as a beginner since it lets you build an eye-catching site without coding a single thing.

So, to help you kickstart your e-learning business, we'll discuss the step-by-step details of creating and selling an online course with Wix.


What Kinds of Courses Can You Create with Wix?

While Wix isn’t technically designed for e-learning, it’s still possible to create good-looking courses you can sell there. You can sell digital products while password-protecting specific pages to only give access to users who've purchased your course.

With Wix, you can make courses that include multi-part video lessons, slideshow lessons, and blog posts. The functionality of these courses will vary based on their:

  1. Length: Create anything from free mini-courses to long multi-module courses
  2. Content: Add audio, video, or PDF files to your courses
  3. Audience: Use Wix Groups to create a members-only area

Additionally, Wix has finally launched its own dedicated app, called Wix Online Programs (originally Wix Challenges), which lets you create online courses. It's available on the Wix App Market and you can use it to create a multi-module course program.

» Building your first site? Check out our top 10 picks for the best website builders.

Create and Sell an Online Course with Wix in 5 Simple Steps

Now for the fun part! Here's a step-by-step guide on how to create and sell an online course with Wix.

1. Plan and Record Your Course

First, you need to plan and present your course. Depending on whether you're doing text, image, or video-based content, you'll need:

  • A high-quality camera
  • A good microphone
  • Lighting gear
  • A screen recording app, if applicable

Pro Tip: Make sure every lesson component is short and digestible. If necessary, record yourself 2-3 times to build confidence when presenting the content.

2. Create a Website With Wix

Once you have your course content ready, you can create your website—unless you already have one. Thankfully, with Wix, building your own website is super easy: you simply need to select a theme and populate it with content.

» Use some of the best Wix templates to inspire your page design.

3. Add Sample Materials and Sales Content on Your Website

Add some sample materials from your course to promote it. For example, you can upload a free lesson or even create a free mini-course to grow your audience. Add PDF materials, information on who your course is best for, whether course-takers need a certain experience level, and what they can achieve with it.

4. Use Wix Online Programs to Upload Your Course

Next, you can add Wix Online Programs to your site, Wix's native app for online courses. With it, you could also sell personal coaching, nutrition plans, or a fitness challenge. You need to decide whether your course will be self-paced or scheduled, or whether there will be any specific challenges and questionnaires.

The app is really simple and intuitive and has tons of useful features. If you need more detailed explanations on how to use it, the Wix Training Academy can explain this in detail.

» Spend less in your first year by trying these money-saving tips for small businesses.

5. Launch Your Course and Sell It

Next, you need to launch your course and sell it. If you already have a social media following or a mailing list, you can promote it to your subscribers. If you don't have any social accounts yet, you should know how to introduce your new business on social media. For example, you can use social media ads to promote your course or even launch a mini-challenge in which you sell your full course at the end.

And remember to always ask people who buy the course whether you could add them to your newsletter. This will enable you to progressively grow your audience and make it easier to sell new courses in the future. Simply adding buyers to your newsletter without asking first is done by many but is not advisable and could get you in trouble with GDPR and similar laws, or get your emails labeled as spam.

Reviews can also help sell your course, so be sure to put them on display to convert your next customers.

And there you go! Now, users can log in to your website and see your course.

What Plan Do You Need to Sell Courses Through Wix?

To sell digital products and accept payments through Wix, you'll need to purchase one of its business and e-commerce plans (Basic, Unlimited, and VIP), which also enable you to upload 5+ hours of video.

As for payment options, here's what you'll need:

Wix Payments

Best for: Selling courses in your local area market

Price: Differs per region but generally 2.9% of the transaction price

Wix has a native payment app called (surprise) Wix Payments which allows you to accept payments from all major credit card companies, including Visa, MasterCard, and American Express, but it's only available in a handful of countries at the moment.

» Learn more about the cost of building a website to help optimize your budget.

PayPal Button

Best for: Selling your courses globally

Price: Free, with paid plans from $4.94/month + PayPal/Stripe fees

If you want to sell your courses globally, you'll need another solution. There are a few other payment apps, but probably the best one of them is the PayPal Button, which you can use to accept payments through PayPal or even integrate it with Stripe.

Bottom Line: Profit

With the global e-learning market exceeding $315 billion in 2021, it's no wonder why so many are scrambling to monetize their knowledge. Wix is one of the best website builders for small businesses. It caters to course creators, too, and does so rather well. So why not use it to make money off of your website using this guide?

articles.title: How to Select the Ideal Website Builder for Your Small Business
articles.subtitle: The right website builder can empower small businesses by building a strong online presence, which is essential in today's digital age.
articles.summary: The right website builder can empower small businesses by building a strong online presence, which is essential in today's digital age.
articles.mainContent:
Website builders enable small business owners to create beautiful websites without spending thousands of dollars on web design. But with so many platforms, picking the right one can be a challenge. And yet, that's one of the most critical choices you'll be making.

How your website looks and feels can significantly impact your business' credibility. According to research in the Journal of Medicine and Life, almost 75% of users judge a website's trustworthiness based on their first impressions of its design, appearance, and ease of navigation.

Let's see how you can pick a website builder for your small business that fits your needs and enforces high design quality, user-friendliness, and security.

» Find out the benefits of having a website for your small business.

Assess Your Business’s Website Requirements

Different website builders cater to different business specifications and budgets, meaning your goals inform your platform choice.

To choose a platform that's best for you, consider the following five questions to help you determine your needs:

1. What's the Main Purpose of Your Website?

You may want to set up a basic company site or start a blog for your business. Luckily, for each type of website, there are suitable platforms. Let's look at some examples.

  • Online store: You should look for a platform with powerful e-commerce capabilities like Shopify or Wix.
  • Image-heavy portfolio website: Squarespace is an intuitive fit since it has countless beautiful templates for this purpose.

2. What's Your Budget?

Different website builders come with different price tags—and you also have the choice between paid vs. free website builders. Compare platform options to weigh up the functionalities you need your site to have against the cost.

3. Are You Planning to Scale Your Business?

If your business is on track to grow rapidly, scalability and security should be a top priority. For instance, see if the platform you're considering has ways to protect your website from cyber-attacks.

Choose a website builder that can support your growth, such as HubSpot, which comes with its own customer relationship management (CRM) platform and marketing suite.

4. How Comfortable Are You With Learning to Use a New Platform?

While you don't need any technical skills or coding knowledge to use a website builder, it's important to consider that some platforms are more complex than others.

If you're a complete newbie, pick a beginner-friendly platform like IONOS or Wix.

5. How Much Storage Space Do You Need?

How much hosting space you need depends on what you plan to upload to your website. Take videos or downloadable content—avoid lowering your website's performance and choose a website builder with higher storage space.

For example, Wix offers multiple solutions with various storage spaces and video bandwidth.

What to Look For in a Website Builder

Factors to consider when choosing a website builder for a small business range from the level of customization you need to the platform's customer support options.

The best small business website builders are user-friendly, affordable, and come with dozens or even hundreds of professionally-designed templates. IONOS is a great choice if you need a budget-friendly option that's super easy to figure out, while Wix's 800+ templates make it ideal for those looking to create a visually diverse website.

5 Key Website Builder Features

1. Customization

If you want to customize every aspect of your website, look for platforms that allow for lots of design freedom. Squarespace is a great choice for this.

2. ECommerce Capabilities

If you plan to add an e-commerce store to your website, you need a website builder with powerful online shopping features, such as Shopify or Wix.

Some of these site builders include:

  • Social media integration
  • Easy and secure checkout processes
  • Customer accounts
  • Built-in shipping calculators

3. SEO Optimization

Optimizing for SEO requires informed strategies that can help boost your site's traffic. Wix is an excellent choice for SEO because it offers various add-on apps which can help you assess site leads, monitor clicks and site traffic, and interact with visitors.

Continuing the focus on SEO optimization, utilizing integrated SEO tools effectively is crucial for enhancing your online presence. Wix not only simplifies SEO through its intuitive interface but also provides specialized apps aimed at maximizing your site’s visibility. These tools are designed to help you analyze your site’s performance metrics, such as visitor interactions, click rates, and lead generation. By leveraging these insights, you can tailor your SEO strategies more precisely, ensuring your website not only attracts but also retains a growing audience.

4. Mobile Responsiveness

With over 54% of global traffic coming from mobile devices, making a site mobile-friendly with responsive design can make or break your site's user experience.

Most website builders now automatically create a mobile version of your website but add this consideration to the list when searching for your ideal website builder.

5. Customer Support

Many platforms give you a few options to contact support for real-time help through live chat or phone support, including a 24/7 callback option in English.

» Discover the types of website navigation for a positive user experience.

5 Tips for Choosing the Right Website Builder

Choosing the right website builder doesn't have to be complicated once you know what you're looking for. Below are my top 5 tips to help you make the right choice:

1. Clearly Define Your Needs and Requirements

Once you know what your website will be for, you can identify the tools you need to manage it successfully. Some needs, depending on the site, can be:

  • Integrations with other apps and platforms, like email marketing integrations
  • Built-in, powerful analytics tools
  • Product management for large inventory selections

Compare your requirements to the features of each platform.

2. Set a Budget and Compare Plans

Most platforms have flexible pricing options to suit different budgets, but always remember to check:

  • Whether the features you need (including web hosting and domain registration) are included in the plan you're considering
  • The price after the first billing period, namely the first month or year, since the increase can sometimes be quite steep

3. Test a Few Platforms

Many website builders have a free trial or even a free version, enabling you to test them. This can show you the extent of a platform's features so you'll know whether it aligns with your needs before you commit.

Look for an intuitive, user-friendly platform with the most helpful templates and customization options.

4. Talk to Customer Support

During the trial period, you can contact customer support to see whether you can get a quick and helpful answer on the first try.

This can be a helpful indicator of how seamless assistance would be if you used this platform long-term.

5. Check Reviews

Check review websites (like ours) and online customers' feedback to see what others think about each platform you're considering. Compare the reviews of a few platforms to get a fuller picture.

And, speaking of feedback, you can try out different customer review templates that you may want to implement for your business.

Use The Right Website Builder To Elevate Your Small Business

Building a website today is no longer the complex process it used to be. With all industries combined holding visitors' attention for an average of 54 seconds, an effective site design can help attract and retain users.

And that's where the right website builder comes in. You'll be able to create a beautiful website for your small business that runs smoothly, targets your goals, and caters to your audience.

articles.subtitle: These days, establishing a robust web presence is crucial for your business to thrive.

articles.mainContent:
The journey begins with choosing the right tools, and a significant first step is selecting the best website builder that enhances your brand's visibility and aligns with your diverse business needs.

As a seasoned web development expert, I've compiled a comprehensive list of 10 essential strategies to grow your business online effectively.

The following insights are designed to guide you through each stage of enhancing your digital footprint, ensuring you have a well-rounded approach to achieving online growth and success.

1. Use a Website Builder

Website builders offer various design possibilities to present your brand attractively and engage your customers. But how do you know which one will work best for you?

Consider these factors when choosing a website builder:

  • Business goals: Ensure the tool aligns with your business objectives and scale. For example, if you want to build an online store, consider an eCommerce website builder.
  • User-friendly design: Think about your brand presentation and user experience. Customization options like animations and scrolling features provide dynamic and appealing elements.
  • Ease of use: Look for a website builder like Wix or GoDaddy that allows you to construct and manage customizable websites with beginner knowledge.
  • Design templates: Check if the platform offers the customizable or website templates for your eCommerce store you need. This can help you create a professional-looking website even if you don’t have design skills.
  • Extensions: Some website builders offer extensions for e-commerce and mailing lists. These can be useful if you plan to sell products or services online or want to build an email list.
  • Cost: Consider your budget. Some website builders offer free plans, but these often come with limitations. Paid plans offer more features and vary in price.

» Here are all the benefits you can expect from having a website for your small business.

2. Create High-Quality Business Site Content

You need high-quality content to attract customers to make your business stand out.

Try these the following tips for high-quality business content creation:

  • Understand your audience: Know your audience’s needs and interests to create content that resonates with them.
  • Create valuable content: Provide value to your audience through education, entertainment, or problem resolution.
  • Use various content types: Use a mix of content types like blog posts, videos, and infographics to engage your audience differently.
  • Measure your success: Use analytics tools to track engagement and improve your content strategy.
  • Equity: Create content that anyone can access and understand. Cater to the hard of hearing or visually impaired to include them in your audience.

» Not quite sure where to start? Try these Wix templates.

3. Optimize Your Website for Search Engines

Without search engine optimization (SEO), your business won't show up on search results when people use Google or Bing.

Try these tips to optimize your website for search engines:

  • Conduct keyword research: Use relevant keywords in your website content to make it easier for users to find.
  • Produce quality content: Include text, images, and videos to engage users and enhance your SEO. Learn how to create high-quality content for marketing success.
  • Populate meta descriptions: Implement meta tags with optimized titles, descriptions, and headers on each page for professional structure. You should also know how to optimize your images.

» Check out our top picks for the best website builders for SEO.

4. Improve Your Business Website Loading Speed

Improving your business website's loading speed involves several key factors. Lastly, enhance loading speed by avoiding excessive plugins and JavaScript code to allow visitors a faster and more efficient user experience.

If you have an eCommerce business, you can consider using a dedicated server to improve your website's loading speed.

5. Optimize Your Site for Mobile Users

When optimizing your website for mobile user experience, it’s essential to put the design first. This includes making elements like the hamburger menu easily visible and ensuring that all items and calls-to-action (CTAs) are easy to find.

Aligning your content in the center can significantly enhance readability on mobile screens, which leads to a better user experience. It’s also essential to establish a clear font hierarchy to improve readability and visual appeal.

Lastly, consider reducing the use of images and videos on the mobile version of your site to develop a smoother browsing flow for your users. By following these best practices, you can create a mobile-friendly site that effectively engages your audience.

» Learn more about making your desktop-only website mobile-friendly.

6. Use Email Marketing to Your Advantage

Email marketing is a powerful tool that can significantly contribute to the growth of your online business. Like planting seeds in a garden, building a loyal customer base through email marketing may take time, but the results can be rewarding.

It’s a timeless method for engaging with your audience and keeping them informed and interested in your brand. Moreover, it is an ideal strategy for sharing content such as promotions, discounts, new blog posts, product launches, events, and other updates.

You can use email marketing to cultivate a thriving business, much like a flourishing garden.

7. Promote Your Business on Social Media

Social media has evolved into a sophisticated field of worldwide digital marketing. Understand the benefits to drive growth and achieve success.

Here are some of the benefits of promoting your website on social media:

  • Reach a global audience: One of the best benefits of social media marketing is that your business can reach your audience on a global scale and grow your customer base.
  • Customer engagement: Social media allows your customers to engage directly with your business businesses, giving the feeling of personal involvement.
  • Brand awareness: Post valuable content regularly to keep your brand in your audiences' minds.
  • Customer feedback: This feedback can help you improve your products or services.
  • Cost-effective marketing: Social media marketing allows you to reach a large audience at a lower cost than traditional marketing strategies.
  • Increased traffic: Sharing content on social media can drive traffic to your website, creating leads to more clicks and increased sales.
  • Competitive advantage: If your competitors are using social media and you’re not, you could miss out on opportunities to reach potential customers.

8. Try Pay-Per-Click (PPC) Advertising

PPC advertising can be worth it for many businesses, including those building their first website.

Here are some reasons why:

  • Fast results: Unlike other advertising forms, PPC can quickly produce results. This can be especially beneficial for a new business looking to attract customers immediately.
  • Targeted advertising: With PPC, you can choose the keywords or phrases that trigger your ads. You'll benefit from targeted ads for people interested in your products or services.
  • Visibility: Even if people don’t click on your ads, they can still see them. This can help increase awareness of your brand.
  • Measurability: With PPC, you can track your business metrics, like how many people saw your ad, how many clicked on it, and more. This knowledge can help you improve your strategy.

9. Start a Blog

It can feel like a challenging task if you are unsure how to start a blog. First, you need to understand its importance for your online business. Blogs are versatile and cater to a wide range of industries, offering a platform to discuss the benefits of your products, share lifestyle tips, and educate your audience.

They contribute to the organic growth of your business by providing valuable and engaging content for your viewers and clients. Blogging establishes authentic and emotional connections with your audience, growing a sense of community around your brand.

10. Retain Online Customers

A few key strategies are involved in retaining your online customers. It’s essential to understand your industry. Customer retention rates vary across different industries, so knowing the average retention rates in your specific industry can help you set realistic and achievable goals.

Personalize your marketing efforts to boost customer retention and satisfaction. By tailoring your marketing strategies to meet your customers' unique needs and preferences, you can build stronger relationships and ensure a more satisfying buying experience.

Achieve Online Success in 2026

Choosing the right website builder is the first and most important step to a successful future. Keep your customers happy and up to date. Remember, success online comes from adapting, engaging, and always giving value to your audience.

Squarespace has excellent built-in SEO, marketing, and analytics features. Its well-designed templates, customizable galleries, and dozens of animation options also make it super versatile. These functionalities enable you to create beautiful, professional websites, even if you have limited design experience.

It has unlimited storage space, making it ideal for sites with many images or videos. With Jimdo, I get everything I need for a website—a domain, template, hosting, and content management system, all in one package. So, I can simply focus on adding content to the site while Jimdo takes care of the rest.

Free Version Options: The presence and quality of free versions are examined to understand how newcomers can benefit without initial investment.

Ease of Use: A key focus is the simplicity and intuitiveness of the platform's interface, ensuring a seamless experience for users of all skill levels.

Design Flexibility: We evaluate the ability to customize and adapt the website's design features, enabling creativity and brand alignment.

E-commerce Capabilities: The support for online selling and business expansion through various e-commerce features is assessed, highlighting platforms that offer robust online store functionalities.

Customer Support: The quality and responsiveness of customer support services are crucial, especially for resolving issues and guiding users.

User Reviews: Real feedback from users is incorporated to gauge satisfaction levels and identify common challenges or praises, providing a user-centric perspective on each alternative.

Through this meticulous process, we aim to deliver an insightful analysis of the best Wix alternatives available, empowering you to make an informed decision based on comprehensive data and in-depth evaluations.

However, with assistance from website builders like Wix, GoDaddy, and WordPress, you can still create a sleek, professionally designed site with restricted finances. I'll use my background in site technical consulting to help you build your website without breaking the bank.

Can You Create a Website for Free?

In short, yes, you can create a website for free, but there will eventually be some maintenance costs.

Many website builders today have a free trial. For example, you can sign up for a free account with Wix to build your website without spending money. Solopreneurs and small businesses commonly use these options to save money in their first year.

One of the most important things to know before you build your website is that offers like these usually have limited features, such as restricted storage space and reduced bandwidth. They may affect the content you can host and the traffic your site can handle.

Additionally, you might not have direct and prompt access to customer support as you get with premium plans, making it challenging to resolve technical issues quickly.

A free website will usually display the name of the building tool you used somewhere in the footer of each page. This can make your site look less professional, which may not align with your branding strategy.

Moreover, free plans can have SEO limitations, potentially affecting your site's visibility on search engines like Google. As a result, your website might fail to reach its full audience potential.

Also, free plans might not offer the best security features. As your website scales, it becomes increasingly important to invest in crucial security features like SSL certificates. This is crucial for maintaining a professional and reliable online presence.

Upgrade options are usually available if you want to grow your business online beyond what the free plan offers. These can provide more storage, better bandwidth, support, and SEO at an additional price.

Website Features You Have to Pay For

While you can build a website for free, there are certain features you will need to pay for. These elements let you design your site, give it an address, and store your files.

For example, you should factor in your annual budget domain name costs, hosting services, and renewal fees.

Set a renewal date in your calendar earlier than the official date, as URLs can expire and be quickly registered by others. Automated reminders can help you avoid losing your domain.

Be aware of hidden fees that may not be apparent at first. These could include charges for (DNS) or transfers. Such expenses can significantly increase the cost of managing your URL over time.

Additionally, consider using subdomains, which are extensions of your main URL. They can be a cost-effective way to expand or organize different sections of your website.

Website Builder Subscription Costs Explained

DIY website builders are inexpensive and can help you get started quickly with a sleek, professional-looking site. Often, they come with simple drag-and-drop functionality and editable templates. These allow you to add various elements in a range of different styles.

Subscriptions often include hosting and a domain name, affecting the overall value and budget. Consider these factors when calculating the total cost of building your website.

Additional features influencing your subscription cost include SEO tools, social media integration, email marketing capabilities, and analytics. These can help you optimize your website and reach a larger audience, but ongoing fees can increase and add up over time.

Lastly, many site builders can integrate with other tools and services, such as customer relationship management (CRM) systems and payment gateways. However, these integrations often require higher-tier plans, which need a bigger budget.

What Increases the Cost of Building a Website?

Website Size or Type

You can use a website builder with a hosting solution for smaller websites, sometimes for free. Compare website builders for small businesses to see which one can offer what you need. Remember to consider future scalability.

A platform that suits a small website now must be revised as it grows, potentially leading to higher costs in the future. If you intend to start a big online store and anticipate a lot of traffic, you may need a VPS (virtual private server). This is a type of hosting service that can handle more site visitors.

Different types of websites require specific functionalities, which can affect the choice of platform and price. For instance, a blog might require strong content management and SEO tools. An optimal one-page website portfolio might need excellent media handling and presentation features. A corporate site might need robust security and data handling capabilities.

Custom Design

While more pricy, professional development offers higher customization, expertise, and potential for a unique and professionally polished web presence. The choice between the two depends on your needs, skills, and budget.

While website builders can help you create your website yourself, they won’t allow you to customize everything—and a quality design is one of the most critical aspects. It can help improve the user experience, which attracts clients and hone your unique brand identity.

If you want a custom site according to the latest web design trends with a unique specific look and features, you’ll most likely need to use the services of a web design company. Though this can be more expensive, it gives you complete control over the style and features of your site. It also allows you to request all the revisions you need to revamp your website down the line.

In addition to the initial design and development costs, it's important to consider ongoing expenses. A custom site may require regular updates, redesigns, or the addition of new features. These can incur additional charges over time but ensure the site remains up-to-date, secure, and functional.

» Take inspiration from these successful brands when designing your website.

Extra Features

Additional features like a PayPal button, a live chat, or a QuickBooks connector usually come with monthly fees. The costs can add up quickly if you need to add a few.

Moreover, integrating external services or platforms, such as CRM systems or email marketing tools, can also add to the overall price. These integrations often require technical expertise to set up and may have their subscription charges.

You should also factor in the ongoing maintenance costs for these features. Regular updates are necessary, and there might be potential compatibility issues. If you want to ensure your website performs well over time, you should also track and monitor website metrics.

How to Reduce Costs

Here are ten tips for creating a website on a tight budget:

  1. Pick a domain name that isn’t taken: The first way to reduce costs is to select a URL you won’t need to buy from someone else.
  2. Choose a cheaper extension: Some, like .inc or .health, are more expensive than others, like .com or .net. Extensions or top-level domains (TLDs) and country-code top-level domains (ccTLDs) come with different price tags.
  3. Compare hosting plans and providers: Compare providers and packages for your needs.
  4. Free or cheap website builder: Find an inexpensive or free version that lets you start.
  5. Use free plugins and tools: Free plugins and tools for SEO, social media integration, and contact forms save you on premium version costs.
  6. Consider shared hosting: If you expect limited website traffic, shared hosting can be more affordable than VPS or dedicated hosting, especially for smaller or start-up websites.
  7. Educate yourself: Learning basic web design and development skills through online resources can reduce the need for professional services.
  8. Plan and budget: Understand what your website needs to help prevent spending on unnecessary features.
  9. Review and adjust plans: Regularly check your subscriptions to ensure you're not paying for more than what is required.
  10. Deals and discounts: Look for special offers, particularly during sale periods like Black Friday or Cyber Monday.

Building a Website Doesn’t Have to Be Expensive

Although affordable, the DIY approach comes with a learning curve. If you don't want to do it all yourself, you can always outsource it to a website builder with a dedicated support team. But, pricing for an outsourced site designer can be considerably more expensive.

Remember, a website is a long-term investment. While initial costs can be low with site builders, it's essential to consider the trade-off between budget and quality. Investing upfront often leads to a more professional, effective, and scalable website.

articles.metaTitle: 10 First Post Ideas to Introduce A Business on Social Media
articles.metaDescription: Introduce your new business on social media the right way with these 10 post ideas to start getting followers and making sales.
articles.title: 10 First Post Ideas to Introduce Your New Business on Social Media
articles.subtitle: Announcing the launch of your business on social media comes with many benefits. It can help you connect with your audience (and first customers!), position your brand among competitors, and help you get your first sales.
articles.summary: Announcing the launch of your business on social media comes with many benefits. It can help you connect with your audience (and first customers!), position your brand among competitors, and help you get your first sales.
articles.mainContent:
If you’re launching a new business, there are plenty of things you need to think about. For example, you have to decide which e-commerce platform to use, how to design your website (Our tip: If you have a limited budget, using a website builder is your best bet), and how to announce your launch on social media. Among the Top 10 Best Website Builders, you’ll find options that suit any budget or need.In this article, we’ll help you with the last part. We’ll discuss 10 first post ideas to successfully introduce your new business on social media so that you can get things going. Social media is becoming a preferred channel of communication for customers, so it’s important to make the most of it when creating your first posts.

Let’s dive in.

1. Introduce Your Business and Mission

If you don’t know where to start, you can simply introduce yourself and your mission. When writing this post, try to answer the following:

  • What is the reason you’ve created this business?
  • What problem does it solve?
  • What is your mission?
  • Who do you want to serve?

It’s always a good idea to accompany a social media post with an image. For this one, you can use Canva to create a beautiful visual that goes with your mission statement and directs your customers to your website in the caption. The benefits of a small business website are plenty, so make sure you have one ready.

2. Showcase Your Products

Another first post idea would be to talk about your products. Choose a beautiful photo of one or more of your products and discuss its benefits.

Here are some examples of what you can discuss:

  • What will it help your customers achieve?
  • How is it better than other products out there?
  • What value does it provide?
  • What does it contain?
  • How is it manufactured or designed?

Most importantly, don’t forget to tell them how they can buy from you!

3. Tell Your Story

Storytelling is one of the most impactful ways to convey your brand's message. What’s more, customers love getting to know the people behind brands, so don’t be afraid to talk about yourself and your story.

Tell your customers about your brand and what inspired you to create it.

4. Promote Your Website

If you’re just launching your business, chances are your website is also brand new. And social media is an excellent place to promote it!

And if you don’t yet have a website, now is the time to get one. There are many great website builders for small businesses, so you are sure to find a platform that suits your needs.

If you’re using Wix, make sure you have the best possible plugins before you announce your website on social media.

5. Provide a Sneak Preview of Your Products

Sneak previews are ideal if you want to create more buzz around your brand before you actually launch. Think about ways to intrigue your audience and create curiosity without telling them what you’re selling just yet.

For example, if you're selling a cleaning product, share a before and after picture to show how effective it is.

6. Launch a Competition

One of the best ways to get more followers is to launch a competition early on. For example, host a competition for the most impressive beard if you sell beard products. If you’re launching a photography service, have a photo contest.

Whatever you decide, don’t forget to:

  • Set clear rules and provide a timeline
  • Offer an awesome prize that potential customers would love
  • Ask participants to share your content and like your page
  • Thank your participants for each submission
  • Ask participants for permission to republish their submissions after the contest

User-generated content is powerful social proof that will help get more eyes on your content. And who doesn't love winning a good prize?

7. Start a Countdown

If you’re looking for ideas and examples on how to introduce your business on Instagram, a countdown might be just what you need! You can create 10 or 15 images with Canva and start a countdown to your launch date, giving a bit more information about your product each day.

If you're using Wix, you can combine this with a countdown plugin for your website by using POWR’s Countdown Timer. You can also use the Outfy plugin to schedule your next posts. You can also use a WordPress plugin if you’re using IONOS or GoDaddy.

8. Split a Large Photo into Multiple Posts

Another way to introduce your business on Instagram is to create a beautiful grid or puzzle consisting of multiple posts that make one large image. Users will need to click on your account to see the full image, creating excitement about your brand. It also nudges users to view your profile and follow you to see how the puzzle will progress, so make sure you choose a beautiful photo for it.

9. Launch a Series

Another way to introduce your new business on social media is to launch a series. For example, you could launch a weekly travel post with user-submitted travel photos, a monthly competition, or a daily Q&A session where you answer your customers' burning questions. If you haven’t gotten any questions yet, you can come up with a few to get the ball rolling.

You can also automatically upload this content on your website by using one of Wix's social media feed plugins.

10. Share the Purpose of Your Product

Your products solve a problem, right? Tell your customers about that!

To announce your business on social media, you can explain how potential customers can use your products to solve a particular problem and get the results they’re after. Talk about the problem in a casual and relatable way to provoke your audience’s interest and save the solution for the end.

Introduce Your Business the Right Way to Get Your First Sales

When you’re launching a new business, creating hype around it using social media is one of the best things you can do to engage with your audience, build brand awareness, and ultimately get your first sales. And before you announce your business on social media, make sure you have everything ready, including your website and all the plugins you need. Utilizing one of the Best Website Builders can help you create a professional and attractive site to support your business launch.

articles.metaDescription: Discover the most cost-effective methods to build your website. Learn the cheapest way to create a website and save money.
articles.title: Budget-Friendly Guide: The Cheapest Way to Create a Website
articles.subtitle: As a business owner, there are already more than enough financially-demanding issues that require your attention. Don't let your website be one of them. While it’s true that building a website will cost you money, it doesn’t need to be expensive.
articles.summary: As a business owner, there are already more than enough financially-demanding issues that require your attention. Don't let your website be one of them. While it’s true that building a website will cost you money, it doesn’t need to be expensive.
articles.mainContent:
The more complex your website, the more expensive it will be. However, if you’re just getting started, there are plenty of ways to optimize your costs. For example, you can use a website builder to design a professional website yourself instead of paying top dollar for a custom-made website.

In this article, we’ll give you 10 tips on building your website on a tight budget and specific advice on how to implement each one.

1. Decide on the Main Purpose of Your Website

The more features your website has, the more expensive it’ll be. This is because some features need to be custom-built. So, it’s smart to define your main objectives before you actually start creating your website. In addition, defining your goals early on will help you stay focused throughout the process and keep costs low.

So, what’s the purpose of your website? Is it:

  • To inform - Do you want to display your company’s portfolio online, along with your contact details? Do you want to provide information on your products or build a blog?
  • To sell - Do you want to create an online store? Do you need a couple of sales pages that are optimized for conversions?
  • To entertain - Do you want to build and entertain an audience?

2. Choose a Cheap Domain Name and Extension

Next, you need to pick a domain name and an extension known as a top-level domain (TLD). Some TLDs can be expensive, like .io, .inc, or .health—but you definitely don’t need those to get started.

Choose a domain name that isn’t taken and an extension that doesn’t cost a lot of money. Be mindful of renewal fees after the first year because these can be steep. In fact, it’s a good idea to opt for a two-year contract if you have the option and check what fees to expect after the two-year period is over.

3. Use a Website Builder

One of the best money-saving tips for small businesses is to use a website builder like Wix, GoDaddy, or SITE123. Using a website builder is an excellent way to create a sleek website on a tight budget. They come with large libraries of templates that you can choose from and a drag-and-drop functionality that’ll help you build and customize your website. Subscription fees range between $7 and $50 per month.

4. Choose a Simple Design Theme

Simpler designs are easier to build and maintain and won’t look outdated next year. If you want to keep costs low, it’s a good idea to choose a simple design theme.

The simpler your design, the easier it will be for visitors to find their way around your website, which is crucial for providing a positive user experience.

Ensure your website has a responsive design to provide a better user experience on all devices.

5. Compare Hosting Plans

While hosting will cost money, it doesn’t need to be expensive. Most hosting providers offer a wide variety of plans suited for different needs.

If you’re just getting started and need a simple website, shared hosting will most likely be sufficient. It’s also the cheapest option, costing as little as $6 per month with reputable hosting providers like Bluehost or GoDaddy. Alternatively, you can also use a website builder that comes with free hosting like Wix.

6. Know How to Do Simple Updates Yourself

Even if you outsource the design of your website, make sure you know how to do simple content updates yourself. Things that you can do on your own include:

  • Making changes to existing content
  • Publishing new blog content
  • Adding new products
  • Updating your prices or applying discounts

So, if you hire a web designer, ask them to show you around the backend of your website and explain how to do these things.

7. Avoid Custom Features

Custom features cost money to design and implement. This is because you need to hire a designer to build them and won’t be able to make changes to them easily.

Most web builders’ ready-made themes come with all the basic features you’ll need to get started, and you can choose your theme based on the purpose of your website.

8. Use Free or Cheap Plugins

Many website builders' plugins have a basic version allowing you to use some of their features for free or for a small fee.

That being said, you probably don’t need too many plugins either—and if you have too many, you risk slowing your website down. So, pick your plugins carefully and use the free version unless you really need the features that come with a paid plan.

9. Use Free Stock Photos

Websites like Unsplash or Pexels feature tons of stock photos you can use on your website free of charge, even for commercial purposes.

What you can’t do is sell the photos—but as long as you use them on your website, that’s fine.

10. Monetize Your Website

What if you could build a website that pays for itself? While that might sound like science fiction to you right now, it’s definitely possible and not that difficult to do.

There are many ways to monetize your website, from affiliate marketing to publishing sponsored content, selling banner ads, or using Google AdSense. Incorporate basic SEO optimization techniques to improve your website’s visibility without extra cost, making it easier to attract traffic and increase your potential revenue from these monetization strategies.

Building a Website Isn't Expensive If You're Smart About It

You don’t need to spend thousands of dollars to build your website. There are plenty of things you can do to optimize your costs and still create a beautiful website that looks professional and delights your visitors—and there are many website builders for small businesses that can help you with that.
